notes:
ROOT CAUSE (established, not assumed): all five red scripts share ONE cause, and it is fixture-side, not detector-side. Each regression fixture stages a new sub-scenario by writing tasks.json DIRECTLY (python json.dump / printf > $STORE), bypassing every managent write path. The S10 census (T848) is only ever advanced by a managent-mediated write, so after fixture arm N's direct overwrite, the committed census still reflects the row count from the LAST managent write in that same script run (an earlier arm's `done`/`add`/`backfill`/auto-done call). The next managent invocation in the fixture — even a nominally read-only one like `lanes`, `status`, or `duty done`, since every invocation persists its migrated state under the same lock — then sees a live count smaller than the stale census and correctly, mechanically, refuses (write path) or alarms (read path). This is exactly the fixture's-own-false-positive failure mode the S10 spec warned about, and it is a fixture defect: a real repository's tasks.json is never hand-written outside managent, so census and store always advance together there; only these test fixtures skip that discipline to stage scenarios. Shown directly: reproduced the regression-managent-lanes.sh arm D sequence by hand in a throwaway scratch repo under /tmp — after arm B's `lanes --backfill` (a real write, census row_count=1) and arm C's direct row injection (bypass, store now 2 rows, census still stale at 1), arm D's direct reset to an empty store made the very next `lanes` call print 'REFUSED: store-loss detector ... live rows: 0 census rows: 1'; deleting the stale store-census.json before that call made the identical `lanes` call print 'lanes: 0 unregistered finding(s), 0 missing-finding row(s)' with exit 0 — isolating the stale census, not the detector's logic, as the cause. The other two candidate readings in the brief do not fit the evidence: the census was never absent (ruling out 'no census yet'), and censusPathFor resolves as a sibling of state_path's own dirname, which the fixture output itself already showed pointing at the fixture's own scratch tasks.json, not the real repo's (ruling out cross-repo path resolution).

FIX: fixture-only, in tools/lib/scratch-repo.sh, a new helper `weizigo_reset_census "$STORE"` that removes the sibling store-census.json. Called immediately after every direct/bypassing write to a scratch tasks.json in the four affected scripts (regression-managent-duty.sh's seed_store, regression-managent-done-two-phase.sh's seed, regression-managent-ledger-board-seam.sh's seed, regression-managent-lanes.sh's three bypass-write sites: the initial truncate, seed_done_row, and the null-control reseed). This puts the store back into the 'no census yet' state — the SAME honest-UNKNOWN path the detector already takes for a brand-new store (checkCensusBeforeWrite/checkCensusRead both return early when `!census.present`) — rather than adding any new conditional, flag, or path-based heuristic to the detector itself. regression-managent-ledger-board-seam.sh did not previously source tools/lib/scratch-repo.sh (a pre-existing T849-doctrine gap); it now does, for this helper. src/managent/main.zig is UNCHANGED — no line of the detector, the write path, or the read path was touched.

UNRELATED DRIFT #1 (lanes null-control failure) TURNED OUT NOT TO BE UNRELATED: tracing regression-managent-lanes.sh arm D showed it is the identical stale-census mechanism (`lanes` also persists migrated state under the write-time check), not a separate binary regression. Fixed by the same weizigo_reset_census call at that script's null-control reseed; no other change was needed or made.

UNRELATED DRIFT #2 (store-pollution's missing --impression/--impression-waiver) is a real, separate, and live gap: tools/runner's worker-channel auto-done (invoked after a lane's clean exit-0) calls `managent done <id>` with no impression flag at all. Since T522's impression-or-waiver gate has no bypass, EVERY auto-done on a real clean-exit lane — not just this fixture's arm C — has been refused since that gate landed; the fixture just happened to be the thing that noticed. Fixed in tools/runner: the auto-done call now passes `--impression-waiver "tools/runner worker-channel auto-done on exit 0 — no model ran to narrate an impression"`, a named, reasoned waiver (never a bypass) consistent with the gate's own no-force-flag design. This is a fix to the caller, not to the gate: `done`'s impression-or-waiver requirement is untouched.

VERIFICATION — both halves:
(1) All five scripts green after the fix, rebuilt zig-out/bin/managent (from HEAD faa5628, unchanged — this task never modified src/managent/main.zig, only the four regression scripts + tools/lib/scratch-repo.sh + tools/runner): regression-managent-duty.sh ALL CHECKS PASS, regression-managent-done-two-phase.sh ALL CONTROLS PASSED, regression-managent-ledger-board-seam.sh ALL CHECKS PASS, regression-managent-lanes.sh ALL CONTROLS PASSED, regression-managent-store-pollution.sh ALL CONTROLS PASSED.
(2) regression-store-census.sh: still ALL 4 ARMS PASSED, unmodified and untouched by this task — the null control, the seeded-defect control (hand-revert refuses the write and alarms the read, naming the missing ids), the reasoned-escape control, and the legitimate-shrink control all still hold exactly as T848 built them.
(3) Live-store protection, proven on a COPY, never the real store: copied the real docs/infra/managent/tasks.json and store-census.json into a throwaway scratch git repo under /tmp, deleted three arbitrary live task ids from the copy only, then ran the built managent binary there. `orient` printed 'ALARM: store-loss detector — live store (483 rows) is smaller than the committed census (486 rows)' naming all three dropped ids by name; `add` on that same copy printed 'REFUSED: store-loss detector' naming the identical three ids and did not write. The real repository's tasks.json and store-census.json were never opened for writing during this reproduction; the real store's row count is unchanged by this task except through managent's own claim/done calls for T855 itself.
(4) Is the detector weaker than before? NO, by construction and by direct test: no line of checkCensusBeforeWrite, checkCensusRead, writeCensus, or any other S10 function in src/managent/main.zig was touched. The fix is entirely in test-fixture setup code (tools/lib/scratch-repo.sh + the four scripts) and in one real caller (tools/runner) that was violating a different, unrelated gate (T522). The five false positives are now false positives no fixture can hit, because the fixtures stopped lying to the detector about being tracked; a genuine revert of the live store (never routed through weizigo_reset_census, which only exists in test tooling and is never invoked against a live MANAGENT_STORE) is caught exactly as before, demonstrated live in (3) above.
